guide.monster_conquest.chapter.rts.body:
#Entering RTS
- Press {key.rts} to enter / leave the RTS command view; the selection is kept, so you can pick up where you left off.
#Selecting
- Left-click a soldier: units in a squad select the whole squad, lone units select only themselves; drag with the left button to box-select.
- Double-click selects every soldier of the same kind (e.g. all zombie soldiers); Ctrl+double-click selects the same troop type (melee / ranged / dual / thrower / gunner, gunners split by gun); Ctrl+click adds to the selection.
- Middle-click switches free / fixed camera.
#Orders (right-click)
- Right-click ground to move, an enemy to attack, a friendly unit to follow it.
#Hotkeys
- Cavalry form {key.cavalry}, infantry form {key.infantry}, formations {key.formation1} ~ {key.formation5}.
- The command wheel ({key.wheel}) offers finer orders.
#Display
- Selected soldiers are marked and the move target is shown on the ground (it fades after about 15 seconds).
guide.monster_conquest.chapter.logic.bod:
#Threat and hatred
- When a unit is attacked or ordered to attack, threat spreads to its army and same-faction reinforcements, so the whole army locks onto the target.
- Hatred does not expire just because a path is long: it only expires when the target is truly unreachable.
- Faction hostility comes from the config and the N-key faction screen; the Hatred Wand adds temporary hostility (Shift+Left-click clears in-game hatred).

#Patrol captains
- A patrol captain spawns with 3 soldiers; while it has fewer than 3, it adopts nearby orphan soldiers of the same faction, never exceeding 3 soldiers in total.
- Adoption drop-off points are safety-checked too (never on roofs, in pits or on hazardous blocks).

#Converting mobs into soldiers
- Commanders and patrol captains can convert the vanilla creatures listed in the config into their own soldiers; each faction has its own toggle under factionConversion in factions-common.toml (undead / illager are on by default, the rest are off).
- A rule may list several target types separated by | and picks one at random, e.g. the illager faction turns pillagers into one of the four gunners.
- Adopting same-faction orphan soldiers is always enabled and is not affected by these toggles.

#Pathfinding
- When you order a unit to a point (single unit move, commander march, squad move), if vanilla pathfinding cannot get there (maze / walls / too long a detour) it automatically switches to a block-level A* route and walks the waypoints out; orders for a whole squad are planned in small batches instead of all on the same tick.
- While marching only the commander plans a route; soldiers queue along the trail it walked and only chase the commander directly when more than 16 blocks behind.
- Units climb ladders / scaffolding / vines: when their goal is above and a climbable block that leads up is right next to them, they climb it; mounted units dismount first and will not remount while climbing.
- Walls and mazes are bypassed with a block-level A* detour: it goes around walls and through wooden doors / fence gates, but never climbs fences or 2+ block ledges.
- A unit that fell behind its follow range paths back first (walking home whenever a route exists) and only teleports when it is truly stuck and no route exists at all.
- Stuck detection combines the absolute distance (am I getting closer?) and the path distance (does a route still exist?):
  - no route at all (e.g. trapped in a pit): after about 10 seconds it escapes upward to an open spot (never next to the enemy);
  - a route exists (even a long detour): treated as a detour, no teleport, only re-planning;
  - truly not moving (blocked by terrain): side steps / doors / dismounting first, then a recovery teleport.
- In combat, an enemy that is unreachable, or clearly higher up (wall top / tower, more than 2 blocks above), is never teleported to: the unit blacklists that target for about 30 seconds and fights what it can reach instead.

#Melee range
- Melee units can only hit enemies on roughly their own level (about 2.4-3 blocks horizontally, at most 1.5 blocks of height difference): standing on a wall or tower keeps you out of melee reach.
- Archers and gunners can still shoot upward; a lance charge allows up to 2 blocks of height difference.

#Mounting
- Soldiers mount on open terrain and dismount in narrow or low passages; they dismount early when the way ahead is too tight for a horse.
- On ladders / scaffolding / vines they never auto-mount or force-mount until they step off the climbable block.

#Peaceful
- On Peaceful difficulty units are not removed, but they gain no hostility or hatred and never attack each other; in-game hatred is cleared.
- To match vanilla monsters, set peacefulRemovesUnits = true in general-common.toml: units are then removed on Peaceful difficulty.
#Features
- Summon commanders, patrol captains and soldiers of any faction with spawn eggs (soldier eggs cycle factions and cavalry / infantry).
- Freshly spawned player-faction soldiers wander naturally: they do not follow you and are never teleported to you until you assign them to a squad or give them an order.
- Command a single unit, a whole army or a whole faction with the Control Tool: move, attack, follow.
- Crouch-right-click a soldier or commander to open the unit screen: inspect its status, manage gear (empty slots = its own gear) and tune strategies for that single unit only.
- Use the command wheel ({key.wheel}) for formations, attacks, movement, riding and squad commands (the recruit-nearby radius is player-common.toml -> enlistNearbyRadius).
- Open the faction screen ({key.faction}) to view and edit hostility and alliances between factions.
- Use the RTS view ({key.rts}) to box-select and command large armies.
- Use the Hatred Wand to mark a unit / faction hostile, or to clear in-game hostility.
- Use the Retrieval Tool to pack a soldier into a spawn egg, keeping faction, form and tier.
- Use the tactical equipment slots ({key.equipment}) for tactical gear: warm clothes (freeze immunity), the horse whistle (summon / ride your war horse) and ammo boxes (ammo reserve).
- Summon your own war horse with the horse whistle; ride form toggles are {key.cavalry} / {key.infantry}.
guide.monster_conquest.chapter.world.bod:
#Village patrols
- Villager patrols spawn naturally with villages: up to 3 per village, each with 1 captain + 3 soldiers (including the four gunners).
- A new squad only spawns while the village has fewer than 3 captains AND there is room for its 3 soldiers within the 9-soldier cap (current soldiers <= 6), so a lost captain is not replaced immediately.
- Spawning only requires the vanilla village check (claimed beds / workstations nearby); villagers are NOT required, so walled-in or buried villagers no longer stop patrols. Spawn positions are safety-checked too.
- Patrols, combat and targeting never leave the village range; when a villager is attacked the patrols defend it like iron golems.
- Only naturally spawned units are affected; spawn eggs, commands and player-recruited units keep their normal behaviour.
- Toggle & tuning: config/monster_conquest/factions-common.toml -> villageSpawn.villager.

#Raid reinforcements
- Each time a raid spawns a new wave, the illager faction immediately sends a random number of patrol squads: they spawn together with that wave's raiders, and the higher the wave, the more squads (up to 5 per wave).
- Reinforcement soldiers come with much better gear: 85% roll above T0 by default (vs 15% for normal summons), weighted towards T3 / T4; tune with raidSpawn.illager.highTierChance.
- Reinforcements count as part of the raid: every reinforcement unit is counted individually in the "raiders remaining" number and boss bar (one-to-one with vanilla raiders).
- Ringing a bell during a raid highlights the reinforcements just like vanilla raiders.
- During a raid, village patrols keep every raid unit locked in their target list (no line of sight needed, no mid-raid drop) until the raid ends.
- Reinforcements patrol, fight and target only near the raid centre; survivors withdraw (despawn) once the raid ends.
- Toggle & tuning: config/monster_conquest/factions-common.toml -> raidSpawn.illager.
guide.monster_conquest.player.note: Every player owns a personal player faction (shown as the player name) and can keep an army; default relations can be edited in the faction screen or the config.
guide.monster_conquest.relations.rules:
- Units of the same or allied factions never attack each other.
- Native peace: illagers never attack vanilla illagers, villagers never attack vanilla villagers or iron golems.
- After an attack the whole army and same-faction reinforcements retaliate, creating army-level hostility.
- The Hatred Wand adds or clears in-game hostility; on Peaceful difficulty no hostility is created.
